name: Harum
overview: Harum was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Koz. The biblical record of Harum is brief, with no additional notes or significant events documented beyond his genealogy. His mention in Scripture serves primarily to establish lineage within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Harum is a proper name meaning 'consecrated.' This meaning reflects a sense of being set apart or dedicated, though the name was not given directly by God according to the record. The significance of the name underscores a biblical theme of consecration within the community of Israel.
familyAndRelationships: Harum is explicitly identified as the son of Koz, who in turn is the son of Aharhel. These relationships establish Harum's place within a Judahite family line, as recorded in the genealogical account of 1 Chronicles 4:8. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Harum's importance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, which trace the heritage and continuity of God's chosen people. While he does not appear in narratives involving major events or roles, his mention as the son of Koz contributes to the biblical emphasis on lineage and God's faithfulness in preserving the tribes of Israel. This genealogical detail supports the broader biblical narrative of God's covenantal promises through the tribe of Judah.
